items.probe_absent_reason: MISSING CAPABILITY: a witness for a session's OWN REASONING PROVENANCE — which does not exist anywhere in this system and is not merely unbuilt here. clears_when asks for a session that was NOT pointed at the mechanism reporting on a due item AND CITING THE BRIEF AS WHERE IT SAW IT. Every artifact a session leaves — a commit, a PR body, an OPEN-ITEMS observation — records what it CONCLUDED, never which input it read to get there, and the criterion turns entirely on that provenance: the identical sentence is the clearing observation from an uncontaminated session and worthless from a prompted one. A probe grepping any of those surfaces for a citation would be reading a self-report as evidence of its own cause. The row also names its own contaminant (the handoff prompt that already told the next session), which no machine can check. This is PERMANENTLY unprobeable under the current artifacts, and would become probeable only if sessions recorded a structured 'read from: session-brief' provenance stamp — which would then be a self-report too, so the honest position is that a human reads it.

items.why_it_is_urgent_despite_being_research: Because it is ALREADY LIVE on the order path, on real money accounts, not sitting behind a mode. Every competing-trade decision the fleet makes today is ranked by a key nobody has measured the outcome of. The old key was WORSE (alphabetical, and provably broken for prefix names), so this is an improvement in kind -- but 'better than an arbitrary rule' is not 'correct', and the gap is currently unmeasured rather than measured-and-small.
items.the_confound_that_makes_it_hard: It is a COUNTERFACTUAL problem: we observe the winner's outcome and never the loser's, so a live correlation between `decided_by` and realised R is confounded by which strategies tend to win under each tier. Only a REPLAY makes the counterfactual observable -- which is why the design routes to backtest_system.py (it runs signals through the REAL aggregate_intents) rather than to a live study. ⚠️ Compounding it: confidence SATURATES -- 1.0 is 20.5% of observations and contenders tie EXACTLY on 50.1% of contests (n=371 conviction_arbitration soak, 2026-06-17..2026-08-30), so half of all contests never reach confidence at all and fall through to the tier below. A pooled number attributed to 'confidence_first' is therefore uninterpretable.

Throughput pp128 22.35 +/- 0.24, tg64 7.19 +/- 0.34 t/s (pre-reboot 22.53 / 7.38 — identical within noise). 36.4s wall, 2.86 GB peak RSS on a 5.9 GB box. THE QUALITY IS THE FINDING, NOT THE SPEED: the sample restated the prompt, FABRICATED a causal claim ('margin was calculated from the per-coin block, indicating that the available balance is less than the required margin' — two unrelated facts joined by an invented 'indicating'), MISATTRIBUTED the fault to venue liquidity when the defect was our own sizer reading an empty account-level field, and TRUNCATED mid-sentence without answering the third of the prompt asking what to check next. A model that confidently invents a cause is worse than no model on a system whose canonical rule is always-verify. THE SIZE EXPECTATION IS ARITHMETIC, NOT A MEASUREMENT — a 3B roughly halves the speed and should raise quality, a 0.5B does the reverse; do not quote either as a result. || 2026-08-31, session ayloee — THE DIFFERENT-SIZE ARM WAS RUN AND THIS ROW DOES NOT CLEAR, BY ITS OWN CRITERION. clears_when says in as many words that a throughput comparison alone does NOT clear it, and a throughput comparison is exactly what came back. Dispatched via LLMBENCH_MODEL_URL (issue #10621) with a dispatch-time positive control; `model:` named the requested Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M URL with NO fallback warning, so the arm is genuine. MEASURED: pp128 10.57 +/- 0.04, tg64 3.91 +/- 0.00 t/s, peak RSS 4,792,340 KB = 4.79 GB on the 5.9 GB box — 2.1x and 1.84x slower than the 1.5B, fitting with ~1.1 GB headroom. NOT MEASURED: the answer. RESULT was `benchmarked_throughput_only`, exit status 124 (timeout), 15:01.52 wall clock, and the captured output is fourteen `>` prompts then `Exiting...` — llama-cli sat in interactive mode and never generated. So nothing whatever may be concluded about 3B answer quality: not 'similar to the 1.5B', not 'presumably worse'. CAUSE, root-caused after two of my own explanations were refuted by measurement (the flag candidate list is NOT stale — `-st` and `--single-turn` are both in build e4b9af0's 562-line help; `--help` does NOT exit non-zero — it exits 0): SIGPIPE. `grep -q` exits on first match, closing the pipe while llama-cli is still writing; llama-cli dies 141 and the script's own `set -uo pipefail` makes the pipeline report 141, so the `if` was FALSE though grep had MATCHED. Measured all three arms (no-pipefail rc=0 / pipefail SKIPPED rc=141 / control TAKEN). Fixed by capturing --help once and matching with `case`. ⚠️ THIS IS THE THREE-STATE CONTRACT WORKING, NOT FAILING: #10597 exists so `benchmarked` is never printed over a generation step that did not run, and it was not — the run graded itself and named which half is valid. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-31: RE-RUN for the answer. It is queued against main once the SIGPIPE fix lands (PR #10620) and costs a full llama.cpp rebuild plus a 2 GB re-download on the 1-core trainer under the heavy lock — the EXIT trap cleaned up, disk back to 7.4 G. || 2026-09-01 (session 01HYXKHpDQeWv3u4rjWWoL2J): THE RE-RUN COMPLETED AND THE ANSWER IS NOW MEASURED — the row is READY FOR THE OPERATOR'S DECISION and is NOT cleared by me, because clears_when ends 'Then the operator decides.' Collected via trainer-diag #10642 off the run launched 2026-08-31T22:11:17Z, finished 22:27:49Z. BOTH CONTROLS PASS, which is what makes the sample gradeable at all: `single-shot flag: -st` (the SIGPIPE fix in #10620 works — the previous run's `benchmarked_throughput_only` is gone) and `RESULT: benchmarked`. DONE marker present, no process running, lock released, EXIT trap cleaned up (disk 7.4G). Throughput on the real generation path: pp128 9.67 +/- 1.27, tg64 3.91 +/- 0.00 t/s; end-to-end 10.5 t/s prompt / 3.7 t/s generation; 200 tokens in 71.07s wall at 96% CPU; peak RSS 4,947,364 KB = 4.95 GB on the 5.9 GB box, ~0.96 GB headroom. Consistent with the earlier throughput-only arm (10.57 / 3.91), so the speed answer has not moved: ~2.1x and ~1.84x slower than the 1.5B.

THE ANSWER, WHICH IS THE DELIVERABLE. Same prompt as the 1.5B baseline. THE 3B IS BETTER ON BOTH SPECIFIC DEFECTS THE 1.5B WAS FAILED FOR, and that is a real improvement rather than a hedge: (1) NO FABRICATED CAUSAL CLAIM — where the 1.5B joined two unrelated facts with an invented 'indicating', the 3B hedges correctly ('This suggests a discrepancy', 'could indicate issues with the margin calculation process'); (2) NO MISATTRIBUTION — the 1.5B blamed venue liquidity, while the 3B keeps the fault on the internal side ('the margin calculation process', 'the margin management system'), which is where the defect actually was. ⚠️ BUT IT NEVER NAMES THE MECHANISM. The real cause is that the sizer fell back to TOTAL EQUITY and counted initial margin already pledged to open positions as free (BL-20260813-ICTSCALP-BTC-BYBIT2-BALANCE-REJECTS, fixed by the coin_derived rung). The 3B produces generic-competent prose that restates the prompt and gestures at 'a discrepancy' — nothing a session could act on. ⚠️ AND CORRECT ONE THING IN THE BASELINE ABOVE: it attributes the 1.5B's truncation to the model ('TRUNCATED mid-sentence without answering the third of the prompt asking what to check next'). THE 3B TRUNCATES AT THE SAME PLACE — 3 complete bullets then a severed '- **Next Steps to' — and the cause is OURS, not the model's: the harness passes `-n 200`, a generation cap both runs hit. Truncation is therefore NOT evidence about either model and must not be counted against the 3B or re-quoted against the 1.5B; raising `-n` is the fix if the 'what to check next' third is ever to be graded.

SO THE MEASURED VERDICT IS: better where it was failed, still not useful, at ~2x the cost and ~1 GB of headroom on a 1-core box. My reading is that this does not carry weight for analysis work on a system whose canonical rule is always-verify — plausible generic prose is the failure mode that rule exists to catch — but the decision is the operator's and the row stays open for it.

Measured 2026-08-31 over trade_journal.db::order_packages (filter_state: applied asserted — that route IGNORES an unknown filter column and silently returns the whole table, which is how a first pass of this same measurement produced five identical wrong numbers): tlt_pullback_1h has n=74 packages 2026-06-22->2026-08-28, 33 of them long (44.6%), against ≤7 packages for every other affordable long-capable leg on the roster, and gdx_pullback_1d at 0 long of 7. WHAT TO EXPECT, so a normal state is not misread as a fault. (a) Roughly HALF this leg's signals will be journalled as suppressed would-be trades: side_filter: long is declared, and independently this is a CASH account with shorting_enabled: false, so the short 55.4% of its flow is structurally unexecutable. Neither is a bug; both are the design.

Declaring a probe today would register a permanent false negative on a REAL-MONEY row. The predicate itself is sound and was checked by hand: that tail spans 2026-07-31->2026-08-31 and holds 80 alpaca_live rows (a real denominator, not zero), all `rejected`, so `account_id=alpaca_live` + `status~open,closed,filled` reads FAIL correctly today and would flip to PASS on the first placement. The 3 existing probes all read /api/diag/log_file envelopes and are unaffected.

items.clears_when: A ping is CONFIRMED to have arrived in @ict_cluade_bot AND NOT in the trader chat. !! DELIVERY IS NOT THE CRITERION AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE. Pings have been delivering throughout -- one enqueued 20:58:49Z on 2026-09-01 was confirmed delivered, to the TRADER chat, while the operator watched the new bot and correctly reported nothing arrived. So 'the ping went out' and 'the drain reported success' clear NOTHING here; the claim is SEPARATION. !! NOR IS THE STARTUP LOG SUFFICIENT ALONE. isolated=True proves which TOKEN the bridge resolved, which is necessary and genuinely new -- but a token is not a conversation, and in a DM the chat_id is the OPERATOR's own id (365546917) for every bot by construction, so the VM side cannot distinguish the two chats even in principle. The last hop is observable only on the operator's phone. Clearing needs BOTH: (a) the startup line reads token=TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET[dedicated] ... isolated=True, AND (b) a human confirms which conversation it appeared in. Either half alone leaves this open.
items.probe_absent_reason: MISSING CAPABILITY, and deliberately NOT a partial probe. The clearing criterion has two halves and only one is machine-observable. The TOKEN half is reachable -- the bridge's startup line is readable via /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-claude-bridge.service and states token=...[dedicated] ... isolated=True. The CONVERSATION half is not reachable from any surface this repo can query, and not for want of an endpoint: in a Telegram DM the chat.id IS the operator's own user id (365546917) for every bot that messages them, so the VM cannot distinguish 'landed in @ict_cluade_bot' from 'landed in the trader chat' EVEN IN PRINCIPLE. The last hop exists only in the operator's app. A PROBE ON THE OBSERVABLE HALF ALONE WOULD BE WORSE THAN NONE, which is why one is not declared. It would go green the moment the token reaches the .env and would render, on the same surfaces that render every other probe, as this row having been checked and found healthy -- while the thing the row exists to establish had never been looked at. That is the exact substitution this row's clears_when spends its length refusing, and a green probe is a far more persuasive way to make it than a sentence in a summary. IF THE CHANNEL EVER MOVES FROM A DM TO A GROUP OR CHANNEL this reason expires: a per-route TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_CHAT_ID would make the destination a distinct id, targets_own_chat would become meaningful, and getUpdates against the dedicated token would be a real probe. Re-file it then rather than assuming this carries.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: The failure mode is a channel that looks healthy from every surface while landing in the wrong place, which is also what a quiet week looks like. Nothing decays into being fixed: the token is either in the VM .env or it is not, and until someone reads the message in the right app nobody can say which conversation it reached.

there_is_no_cap: Deliberately UNCAPPED (operator-directed 2026-08-26: 'we don't want to cap the number of bugs we can track, we want to ensure that they are actually being tracked, fixed, and learned from'). An earlier version capped this at 12 rows; that was a bandaid — it bounded the LIST rather than making anything get read or fixed. What bounds it instead is that a `monitoring` row must be RE-OBSERVED on a cadence: it cannot be carried by doing nothing.
monitoring_rows_are_enforced_by_observat: kind:'monitoring' rows carry `check_every_days`, `verified_at` and `observation`. A row past its cadence is DUE and is rendered into CLAUDE.md, so the next session sees it in context before acting. Clearing it for another cycle costs one honest look: record WHAT YOU OBSERVED and today's date. It cannot be cleared by asserting progress — `observation` must state a thing that was seen. This replaces `loud`, which was just another alarm to walk past.
probes_report_they_never_clear: A `monitoring` row may carry `probe` (a declared command that OBSERVES something, run by scripts/ops/run_probes.py) or `probe_absent_reason` (why none exists), never both and never neither — so 'nothing probes this' stays distinguishable from 'a probe ran and was quiet'. A probe REPORTS; only a SESSION clears a row. Every probe therefore declares `is_not`: what a PASS still does not establish. The hazard is not a broken probe, it is a working one read as proof the row cleared.
